description: GitHub's hosted macos-15 runners: every macos.yml job sets BTRC_TEST_RUNNER=macos-hosted (Stage 38, CL-R-36). A hosted runner expects only platform skips (tests for another OS or toolchain) and hardware skips (a device the image lacks, covered by the acceptance Mac); tools/qualification/skips.py enforces both. Classified from macOS runs 37110991739 (main, 5b57618) and 37099829848 (stage30/ci-codex-lanes, 379ab93): unit 86 and btrc 3 skips, the corpus, bootstrap and strict-C11 shards none, all of them platform. Unlike the acceptance Mac, a hosted runner has no capability or runtime-probe rule: macos.yml enables developer mode, so a DAP session skip is a defect, ThreadSanitizer starts there, and clang's ASan+UBSan runtime runs. The two hardware rules matched nothing in those runs.

rules.note: windows.yml runs test_artifact_storage.py on a native Windows host.
windows.yml runs test_bootstrap_harness.py before its native bootstrap.
macOS resolves the cache under ~/Library/Caches; the XDG branch is Linux behavior.
These cases link ELF objects with the Linux toolchain.

rules.reason: ^requires Linux and the explicitly built native header reader$
rules.note: Image decoding, FreeType rasterization and audio fault injection need no display or PCM, the devcontainer's image installs a null default PCM (nix/asound.conf) for the audio sessions, and CI runs every Linux shard under tools/virtual-display.sh (Xvfb and Mesa lavapipe) for the GUI windows and the GPU view, so the devcontainer runs all eight.

rules.reason: ^the call shapes are proven against glibc$
rules.note: glibc's transparent-union socket addresses, its variadic fcntl and the native tag aliases are proven against the Linux dev shell's sysroot through both frontends; the devcontainer's unit shard runs every case.
tools/ui/headless-session.sh starts Xvfb or weston with the AT-SPI bus from the Linux dev shell; the devcontainer's unit shard runs every case.

rules.reason: ^the (FreeType proof builds against the Linux SDK|macro proof builds against the Linux C toolchain|WebGPU proof builds against the Linux SDK)$
rules.note: The macro-constant proofs build against the Linux dev shell's C toolchain, freetype2 (pkg-config) and WebGPU headers; the devcontainer's unit shard runs both frontends (CI run 36935218617 for FreeType).

rules.reason: ^requires Linux and the explicitly built native header reader$
rules.note: The tray also needs a StatusNotifierItem watcher on a session bus, which the devcontainer lacks.
The configured-PCM capability cases run wherever ALSA headers exist.

rules.reason: ^(gcc cannot link ASan\+UBSan here: ld: library not found for -lasan|compiler wrapper does not provide its UBSan runtime$)
rules.note: GCC ships no libsanitizer for aarch64-darwin, so the dev shell's gcc links neither -lasan nor its UBSan runtime on macOS. Only the gcc parametrizations are expected: the same ASan+UBSan witness and UBSan freestanding cases run through clang and /usr/bin/clang on this runner (macOS runs 37110991739 and 37099829848), and through gcc in the devcontainer (CI 37110991727).

CoreAudioDeviceConformance.btrc prints these when the host has no usable default output device (no output stream with a known 16 to 8,192 frame buffer) or the device refuses an output session (unavailable, busy or permission denied). A hosted image's audio device is not guaranteed; the acceptance Mac's built-in output runs the callback and drain barrier. The provider itself must still open: 'CoreAudio provider unavailable' stays unexpected here.

The harness exits 77 when wgpu-native finds no compute adapter. Hosted macos-15 exposes a paravirtual Metal adapter, so these cases ran there in macOS runs 37110991739 and 37099829848; the rule keeps a runner image without one from failing the gate, and the acceptance Mac's GPU covers them. The WebGPU toolchain itself is required: its skips stay unexpected.

rules.reason: ^the oracle compares against the host's own C preprocessor$
rules.note: The C oracle compares btrc's linux-x86_64 selection with the host gcc and clang -E, so only an x86_64 Linux host runs it; the devcontainer does (CL-C-06).

rules.reason: ^Mac-bound: requires macOS with xcrun and Xcode 27A266a \(MAC-P1-05\); this host has
rules.note: platform-target-contract.md §1.3 pins Apple clang's TARGET_OS_* set and the iOS SDK's <TargetConditionals.h> to the acceptance Mac's Xcode 27A266a; a hosted image carries another Xcode, whose predefined TARGET_OS_* set may differ. MAC-P1-05 runs both checks on the acceptance Mac; a hosted platform rule cannot name that host in covered_by, so the report shows them uncovered here.
CX-UIA-09 shell requires its host provider; both frontends and sanitizer modes run on the named stand-in.
